apatosaurus:enwiki:5.title: Apatosaurus (Second Dinosaur Rush and skull issue)

apatosaurus:enwiki:6.title: Apatosaurus (Second Dinosaur Rush and skull issue, part 2)

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh described and named the genus Apatosaurus in 1877.
facts.quote: authority: Marsh, 1877

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Apatosaurus ajax.
facts.quote: type_species: Apatosaurus ajax

facts.statement: The species Apatosaurus louisae was described by Holland in 1916.
facts.quote: subdivision: *A. louisaeHolland, 1916

facts.statement: Marsh named the first known species, Apatosaurus ajax, in 1877.
facts.quote: Othniel Charles Marsh described and named the first-known species, Apatosaurus ajax, in 1877

facts.statement: Apatosaurus lived approximately 152 to 151 million years ago during the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus lived about 152 to 151 million years ago (mya), during the late Kimmeridgian to early Tithonian age

facts.statement: Fossils of Apatosaurus have been found in the Morrison Formation across Colorado, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Wyoming, and Utah.
facts.quote: are now known from fossils in the Morrison Formation of modern-day Colorado, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Wyoming, and Utah in the United States

facts.statement: The average length of Apatosaurus was 21 to 23 meters, with an average mass of 16.4 to 22.4 tonnes.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus had an average length of 21 - 23 m, and an average mass of 16.4 - 22.4 t

facts.statement: Apatosaurus belongs to the diplodocid family of sauropod dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus is a member of the diplodocid family

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had less elongated and more heavily constructed cervical vertebrae compared to Diplodocus.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebrae of Apatosaurus are less elongated and more heavily constructed than those of Diplodocus

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had air sacs that made its vertebrae internally porous to reduce weight.
facts.quote: To lighten its vertebrae, Apatosaurus had air sacs that made the bones internally full of holes

facts.statement: It is debated whether Brontosaurus is a distinct genus from Apatosaurus, as a 2015 study supports the distinction but not all paleontologists agree.
facts.quote: A 2015 study concluded that Brontosaurus is a valid genus of sauropod distinct from Apatosaurus, but not all paleontologists agree with this division

facts.statement: Most size estimates for Apatosaurus are based on specimen CM 3018, which measures 21 to 23 meters in length and weighs 16.4 to 22.4 tonnes.
facts.quote: Most size estimates are based on specimen CM 3018, the type specimen of A.louisae, reaching 21 - 23 m in length and 16.4 - 22.4 t in body mass

facts.statement: A 2015 study estimated the mass of specimen CM 3018 to be between 21.8 and 38.2 tonnes using volumetric models.
facts.quote: A 2015 study that estimated the mass of volumetric models of Dreadnoughtus, Apatosaurus, and Giraffatitan estimates CM 3018 at 21.8 - 38.2 t

facts.statement: The previously high size estimate for specimen OMNH 1670 was revised in 2020 to 30 meters in length and 33 tonnes in mass based on volumetric analysis.
facts.quote: The upper size estimate of OMNH 1670 is likely an exaggeration, with the size estimates revised in 2020 at 30 m in length and 33 MT in body mass based on volumetric analysis

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had spatulate, chisel-like teeth suited for an herbivorous diet.
facts.quote: The jaws are lined with spatulate (chisel-like) teeth suited to an herbivorous diet

facts.statement: In Apatosaurus louisae, the atlas-axis complex of the first cervical vertebrae is nearly fused.
facts.quote: In Apatosaurus louisae, the atlas-axis complex of the first cervicals is nearly fused

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had ten dorsal ribs on each side of its body.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus has ten dorsal ribs on either side of the body

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had very long ribs compared to other diplodocids, resulting in an unusually deep chest.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus also had very long ribs compared to most other diplodocids, giving it an unusually deep chest

facts.statement: The humerus of Apatosaurus is stout and resembles those of Camarasaurus and Brontosaurus.
facts.quote: The arm bones are stout, so the humerus of Apatosaurus resembles that of Camarasaurus, as well as Brontosaurus

facts.statement: Charles Gilmore noted in 1936 that Apatosaurus forelimb bones (radius and ulna) remained parallel in life, contrary to earlier reconstructions.
facts.quote: In 1936, Charles Gilmore noted that previous reconstructions of Apatosaurus forelimbs erroneously proposed that the radius and ulna could cross; in life they would have remained parallel

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had a foot digit formula of 3-4-5-3-2, with three claws on the innermost digits.
facts.quote: The foot of Apatosaurus has three claws on the innermost digits; the digit formula is 3-4-5-3-2

facts.statement: Brontosaurus is the only other genus in the subfamily Apatosaurinae, with other genera considered synonyms or reclassified as diplodocines.
facts.quote: Only Brontosaurus is also in the subfamily, with the other genera being considered synonyms or reclassified as diplodocines

facts.statement: The first Apatosaurus fossils were discovered in 1877 in Morrison, Colorado, by miner Arthur Lakes and his friend Henry C. Beckwith.
facts.quote: The first Apatosaurus fossils were discovered by Arthur Lakes, a local miner, and his friend Henry C. Beckwith in the spring of 1877 in Morrison, a town in the eastern foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Jefferson County, Colorado.

facts.statement: A well-preserved partial postcranial skeleton with many vertebrae and a partial braincase, collected in 1877, was named Apatosaurus ajax in November 1877.
facts.quote: One of the best specimens collected by Lakes in 1877 was a well preserved partial postcranial skeleton, including many vertebrae, and a partial braincase (YPM VP 1860), which was sent to Marsh and named Apatosaurus ajax in November 1877.

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh named the genus Apatosaurus based on the similarity of its chevron bones to those of the mosasaur Mosasaurus.
facts.quote: Marsh gave it this name based on the chevron bones, which are dissimilar to those of other dinosaurs; instead, the chevron bones of Apatosaurus showed similarities with those of mosasaurs, most likely that of the representative species Mosasaurus.

facts.statement: All known Apatosaurus specimens come from the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: All specimens currently considered Apatosaurus were from the Morrison Formation, the location of the excavations of Marsh and Cope.

facts.statement: Elmer Riggs described a well-preserved diplodocid skeleton (Field Museum specimen P25112) from the Grand River Valley near Fruita, Colorado, in 1903.
facts.quote: In 1903, Elmer Riggs published a study that described a well-preserved skeleton of a diplodocid from the Grand River Valley near Fruita, Colorado, Field Museum of Natural History specimen P25112.

facts.statement: Elmer Riggs concluded that Brontosaurus is a junior synonym of Apatosaurus because Apatosaurus was named earlier.
facts.quote: Since Apatosaurus was the earlier name, Brontosaurus should be considered a junior synonym of Apatosaurus.

facts.statement: The first Apatosaurus skull was found in 1909 by Earl Douglass at the Carnegie Quarry in Dinosaur National Monument.
facts.quote: It was not until 1909 that an Apatosaurus skull was found during the first expedition, led by Earl Douglass, to what would become known as the Carnegie Quarry at Dinosaur National Monument.

facts.statement: After William H. Holland's death in 1934, museum staff replaced the missing head on the Carnegie Apatosaurus mount with a cast of a Camarasaurus skull.
facts.quote: After Holland's death in 1934, museum staff placed a cast of a Camarasaurus skull on the mount.

facts.statement: On October 20, 1979, the Carnegie Museum mounted the first true Apatosaurus skull on a skeleton.
facts.quote: On October 20, 1979, after the publications by McIntosh and Berman, the first true skull of Apatosaurus was mounted on a skeleton in a museum, that of the Carnegie.

facts.statement: In 1998, it was suggested that the skull Marsh used in his 1896 restoration from Felch Quarry actually belonged to Brachiosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1998, it was suggested that the Felch Quarry skull that Marsh had included in his 1896 skeletal restoration instead belonged to Brachiosaurus.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest Apatosaurus might have had a Camarasaurus-like skull, based on a disarticulated tooth found at an Apatosaurus site.
facts.quote: Even though they supported Holland, it was noted that Apatosaurus might have possessed a Camarasaurus-like skull, based on a disarticulated Camarasaurus-like tooth found at the precise site where an Apatosaurus specimen was found years before.

facts.statement: Despite being scientifically invalid, the name Brontosaurus became widely used in popular culture for Apatosaurus due to the American Museum of Natural History's popular mount.
facts.quote: Because of this decision the name Brontosaurus was commonly used outside of scientific literature for what Riggs considered Apatosaurus, and the museum's popularity meant that Brontosaurus became one of the best known dinosaurs, even though it was invalid throughout nearly all of the 20th and early 21st centuries.

facts.statement: Marsh originally distinguished Apatosaurus from Atlantosaurus based on the number of sacral vertebrae, claiming Apatosaurus had three while Atlantosaurus had four.
facts.quote: Marsh distinguished the new genus Apatosaurus from Atlantosaurus on the basis of the number of sacral vertebrae, with Apatosaurus possessing three and Atlantosaurus four.

facts.statement: Recent research suggests that the traits Marsh used to distinguish Apatosaurus from Atlantosaurus were widespread, rendering many such taxa invalid.
facts.quote: Recent research shows that traits usually used to distinguish taxa at this time were actually widespread across several taxa, causing many of the taxa named to be invalid, like Atlantosaurus.

facts.statement: The skulls used to create the Apatosaurus mount were likely from Camarasaurus, as it was the only sauropod with known skull material at the time.
facts.quote: These skulls were likely those of Camarasaurus, the only other sauropod for which good skull material was known at the time.

facts.statement: Elmer Riggs determined that the distinguishing features between Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus were invalid because the holotype of Apatosaurus ajax was immature.
facts.quote: Most of the skeleton was found, and after comparison with both Brontosaurus and Apatosaurus ajax, Riggs realized that the holotype of A.ajax was immature, and thus the features distinguishing the genera were not valid.

facts.statement: The first Apatosaurus specimen with an articulated skull and cervical vertebrae was described in 2011.
facts.quote: In 2011, the first specimen of Apatosaurus where a skull was found articulated with its cervical vertebrae was described.

facts.statement: Specimen CMC VP 7180 differs in skull and neck features from Apatosaurus louisae but shares cervical vertebrae features with Apatosaurus ajax.
facts.quote: This specimen, CMC VP 7180, was found to differ in both skull and neck features from A.louisae, but shared many features of the cervical vertebrae with A.ajax.

facts.statement: Brigham Young University specimen 17096 is a well-preserved Apatosaurus skull and skeleton that includes a preserved braincase.
facts.quote: Another well-preserved skull is Brigham Young University specimen 17096, a well-preserved skull and skeleton, with a preserved braincase.

facts.statement: Most modern paleontologists agree that Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus should be classified as a single genus.
facts.quote: Almost all modern paleontologists agreed with Riggs that the two dinosaurs should be classified together in a single genus.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Robert T. Bakker argued in the 1990s that Apatosaurus excelsus should be classified as a separate genus distinct from Apatosaurus ajax.
facts.quote: Despite this, at least one paleontologist – Robert T. Bakker – argued in the 1990s that A.ajax and A.excelsus were in fact sufficiently distinct for the latter to merit a separate genus.

facts.statement: In 2015, Tschopp, Mateus, and Benson proposed criteria using thirteen characters for generic separation and six for species separation in diplodocoids.
facts.quote: In 2015, Emanuel Tschopp, Octávio Mateus, and Roger Benson released a paper on diplodocoid systematics, and proposed that genera could be diagnosed by thirteen differing characters, and species separated based on six.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus species are distinguished from Brontosaurus excelsus by having a wider and presumably stronger neck.
facts.quote: Among the many notable differences are the wider – and presumably stronger – neck of Apatosaurus species compared to B.excelsus.

facts.statement: Many Apatosaurus species were named by Marsh based on fragmentary and indistinguishable remains.
facts.quote: Many species of Apatosaurus have been designated from scant material. Marsh named as many species as he could, which resulted in many being based upon fragmentary and indistinguishable remains.

facts.statement: Paul Upchurch and colleagues published a 2005 study analyzing species and specimen relationships within Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2005, Paul Upchurch and colleagues published a study that analyzed the species and specimen relationships of Apatosaurus.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus ajax was named by Marsh in 1877 after Ajax, a hero from Greek mythology.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus ajax was named by Marsh in 1877 after Ajax, a hero from Greek mythology.

facts.statement: Specimens assignable to Apatosaurus ajax date from the late Kimmeridgian to the early Tithonian ages.
facts.quote: The specimens date from the late Kimmeridgian to the early Tithonian ages.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus louisae was named by Holland in 1916 based on a partial skeleton found in Utah.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus louisae was named by Holland in 1916, being first known from a partial skeleton that was found in Utah.

facts.statement: The holotype for Apatosaurus louisae is CM 3018, with referred specimens including CM 3378, CM 11162, and LACM 52844.
facts.quote: The holotype is CM 3018, with referred specimens including CM 3378, CM 11162, and LACM 52844.

facts.statement: All Apatosaurus louisae specimens originate from the late Kimmeridgian of Dinosaur National Monument.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus louisae specimens all come from the late Kimmeridgian of Dinosaur National Monument.

facts.statement: In 2015, Tschopp et al. determined that the type specimen of Apatosaurus laticollis is likely a junior synonym of Apatosaurus louisae.
facts.quote: In 2015, Tschopp et al. found the type specimen of Apatosaurus laticollis to nest closely with CM 3018, meaning the former is likely a junior synonym of A.louisae.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus grandis was named by Marsh in 1877 in the same article that described Apatosaurus ajax.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus grandis was named in 1877 by Marsh in the article that described A.ajax.

facts.statement: Because Morosaurus is a synonym of Camarasaurus, Camarasaurus grandis is the oldest-named species of that genus.
facts.quote: Since Morosaurus has been considered a synonym of Camarasaurus, C.grandis is the oldest-named species of the latter genus.

facts.statement: Elmer Riggs reclassified Brontosaurus as a synonym of Apatosaurus in 1903, transferring Brontosaurus excelsus to Apatosaurus excelsus.
facts.quote: Elmer Riggs reclassified Brontosaurus as a synonym of Apatosaurus in 1903, transferring the species B.excelsus to A.excelsus.

facts.statement: In 2015, Tschopp, Mateus, and Benson reclassified Apatosaurus excelsus back into the genus Brontosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2015, Tschopp, Mateus, and Benson argued that the species was distinct enough to be placed in its own genus, so they reclassified it back into Brontosaurus.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus parvus was first described as Elosaurus in 1902, reassigned to Apatosaurus in 1994, and then to Brontosaurus in 2015.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus parvus, first described from a juvenile specimen as Elosaurus in 1902 by Peterson and Gilmore, was reassigned to Apatosaurus in 1994, and then to Brontosaurus in 2015.

facts.statement: Henry Mook named Apatosaurus minimus as a distinct species in 1917 based on a pair of ilia and their sacrum.
facts.quote: In 1917, Henry Mook named it as its own species, A.minimus, for a pair of ilia and their sacrum.

facts.statement: In 2012, Taylor and Wedel found the material of Apatosaurus minimus difficult to place within Diplodocoidea or Macronaria.
facts.quote: In 2012, Mike P. Taylor and Matt J. Wedel published a short abstract describing the material of A. minimus, finding it hard to place among either Diplodocoidea or Macronaria.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus minimus was thought to represent a form with convergent features from many groups rather than belonging clearly to Saltasaurus.
facts.quote: While it was placed with Saltasaurus in a phylogenetic analysis, it was thought to represent instead some form with convergent features from many groups.

facts.statement: Tschopp et al. found a camarasaurid position for Apatosaurus minimus supported but noted its phylogenetic position was highly variable.
facts.quote: The study of Tschopp et al. did find that a camarasaurid position for the taxon was supported, but noted that the position of the taxon was found to be highly variable and there was no clearly more likely position.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus alenquerensis was named in 1957 by Albert-Félix de Lapparent and Georges Zbyweski.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus alenquerensis was named in 1957 by Albert-Félix de Lapparent and Georges Zbyweski.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus alenquerensis was based on post-cranial material from Portugal.
facts.quote: It was based on post cranial material from Portugal.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus alenquerensis was reassigned to Camarasaurus in 1990 and then given its own genus, Lourinhasaurus, in 1998.
facts.quote: In 1990, this material was reassigned to Camarasaurus, but in 1998 it was given its own genus, Lourinhasaurus.

facts.statement: Tschopp et al. (2015) supported the classification of Lourinhasaurus as sister to Camarasaurus and other camarasaurids.
facts.quote: This was further supported by the findings of Tschopp et al. in 2015, where Lourinhasaurus was found to be sister to Camarasaurus and other camarasaurids.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus yahnahpin was named by James Filla and Patrick Redman in 1994.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus yahnahpin was named by James Filla and Patrick Redman in 1994.

facts.statement: Bakker made Apatosaurus yahnahpin the type species of Eobrontosaurus in 1998, and Tschopp reclassified it as Brontosaurus yahnahpin in 2015.
facts.quote: Bakker made A.yahnahpin the type species of a new genus, Eobrontosaurus in 1998, and Tschopp reclassified it as Brontosaurus yahnahpin in 2015.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus is sometimes classified in the subfamily Apatosaurinae, a group that may also include Suuwassea, Supersaurus, and Brontosaurus.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus is sometimes classified in the subfamily Apatosaurinae, which may also include Suuwassea, Supersaurus, and Brontosaurus.

facts.statement: In 1878, Othniel Charles Marsh raised the family containing Apatosaurus to the rank of suborder, including Apatosaurus, Atlantosaurus, Morosaurus, and Diplodocus.
facts.quote: In 1878, Marsh raised his family to the rank of suborder, including Apatosaurus, Atlantosaurus, Morosaurus (=Camarasaurus) and Diplodocus.

facts.statement: In 1903, Elmer S. Riggs grouped Apatosaurus within Opisthocoelia, arguing that the name Sauropoda was a junior synonym of earlier names.
facts.quote: In 1903, Elmer S. Riggs said the name Sauropoda would be a junior synonym of earlier names; he grouped Apatosaurus within Opisthocoelia.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Jurásico Superior

facts.statement: Apatosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately between 155.7 and 150.8 million years ago in the Kimmeridgian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus (gr. "lagarto engañoso") es un género con dos especies conocidas extintas de dinosaurio saurópodo diplodócido, que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 155,7 y 150,8 millones de años, en el Kimmeridgiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus was the first large sauropod whose complete skeleton was exhibited to the public.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus, fue el primer gran saurópodo cuyo esqueleto completo se expuso al público.

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh described and named the first known species, Apatosaurus ajax, in 1877, while William H. Holland discovered and named a second species, Apatosaurus louisae, in 1916.
facts.quote: Othniel Charles Marsh describió y nombró la primera especie conocida, Apatosaurus ajax en 1877 y una segunda especie, Apatosaurus louisae, fue descubierta y nombrada por William H. Holland en 1916.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus lived about 152 to 151 million years ago during the early Tithonian, and fossils are known from the Morrison Formation in present-day Colorado, Oklahoma, and Utah, USA.
facts.quote: Vivieron hace unos 152 a 151 millones de años, durante el Titoniano temprano, y se conocen a partir de fósiles en la formación Morrison de la actual Colorado, Oklahoma y Utah, en Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had a length between 21 and 22.8 meters and a mass between 16.4 and 22.4 tonnes.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus tenía una longitud entre 21 a 22,8 metros, y una masa entre 16,4 a 22,4 toneladas.

facts.statement: Some specimens indicate a maximum length up to 11-30% greater than the average and a mass between 32.7 and 72.6 tonnes.
facts.quote: Unos ejemplares indican una longitud máxima de 11-30 % mayor que la media y una masa entre 32,7 a 72,6 toneladas.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had less elongated and more heavily built cervical vertebrae than Diplodocus, and more robust leg bones despite being longer, implying it was a more robust animal.
facts.quote: Las vértebras cervicales de Apatosaurus son menos alargadas y más pesadamente construidas que las de Diplodocus, un diplodócido como Apatosaurus, y los huesos de la pierna son mucho más robustos a pesar de ser más largos, lo que implica que Apatosaurus era un animal más robusto.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus had a single claw on each forelimb and three claws on each hind limb.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus tenía una sola garra en cada extremidad anterior y tres en cada uno de los miembros posteriores.

facts.statement: To lighten its vertebrae, Apatosaurus had air sacs that made the internal bones full of holes.
facts.quote: Para aligerar sus vértebras, Apatosaurus tenía sacos de aire que hicieron los huesos internos llenos de agujeros.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus was a generalist herbivore that probably carried its head elevated.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus era un herbívoro generalista que probablemente llevaba su cabeza elevada.

facts.statement: Like other diplodocids, the tail of Apatosaurus may have been used as a whip to create loud noises.
facts.quote: Al igual que la de otros diplodócidos, la cola puede haber sido utilizado como un látigo para crear ruidos fuertes.

facts.statement: Stevens and Parish (2005) speculate that sauropods like Apatosaurus fed from riverbanks on submerged water plants.
facts.quote: Stevens and Parish (2005) speculate that these sauropods fed from riverbanks on submerged water plants.

facts.statement: A 2015 study found that variations in the necks of Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus may have been used for intraspecific combat.
facts.quote: A 2015 study of the necks of Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus found many differences between them and other diplodocids, and that these variations may have shown that the necks of Apatosaurus and Brontosaurus were used for intraspecific combat.

facts.statement: Studies by Taylor argue that Apatosaurus would have held its neck at maximum vertical extension in an alert posture, barring unknown unique characteristics in soft tissue anatomy.
facts.quote: Other studies by Taylor find that all tetrapods appear to hold their necks at the maximum possible vertical extension when in a normal, alert posture; they argue the same would hold true for sauropods barring any unknown, unique characteristics that set the soft tissue anatomy of their necks apart from that of other animals.

facts.statement: Taylor disputes the conclusions of Cobley et al., finding that the neck of Apatosaurus was very flexible based on intervertebral cartilage analysis.
facts.quote: The conclusions of Cobley etal. are disputed by Taylor, who analyzed the amount and positioning of intervertebral cartilage to determine the flexibility of the neck of Apatosaurus and Diplodocus. He found that the neck of Apatosaurus was very flexible.

facts.statement: While a 2015 study concluded Brontosaurus was a valid genus distinct from Apatosaurus, not all paleontologists agree with this division.
facts.quote: El término Brontosaurus ha sido considerado como un sinónimo más moderno de Apatosaurus y su única especie, se reclasificó como A. excelsus en 1903. Sin embargo, un estudio de 2015 concluyó que Brontosaurus era un género de saurópodo válido distinto de Apatosaurus. Sin embargo, no todos los paleontólogos están de acuerdo con esta división.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus was a large quadruped with a long neck and a long whip-like tail.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus era un gran animal cuadrúpedo de cuello largo, con una larga cola en forma de látigo.

facts.statement: Its front legs were slightly shorter than its hind legs.
facts.quote: Sus patas delanteras eran ligeramente más cortas que las traseras.

facts.statement: They reached nearly 23 meters in length, 4.5 meters high at the hips, and weighed 22 tonnes.
facts.quote: alcanzaban cerca de 23 metros de largo, 4,5 de alto hasta las caderas y tenían un peso de 22 toneladas.

facts.statement: The tail was held off the ground during normal locomotion.
facts.quote: La cola se mantenía despegada del suelo durante la locomoción normal.

facts.statement: Like most sauropods, it had only one large claw on each front foot and three clawed toes on the hind foot.
facts.quote: Como la mayoría de los saurópodos, Apatosaurus tenía solo una garra grande en cada pata delantera, con los tres primeros dedos de la extremidad posterior con garras.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Apatosaurus may have swallowed stones called gastroliths to help digest tough plant fibers because its jaws could not chew them effectively.
facts.quote: Para ayudar en el proceso del alimento, el Apatosaurus pudo haber tragado piedras, gastrolitos, de la misma manera que lo hacen muchos pájaros, ya que sus quijadas por sí solas no eran suficientes para masticar las resistentes fibras de las plantas.

facts.statement: The holotype of A. louisae has a vertebral formula of 15 cervical, 10 dorsal, 5 sacral, and 82 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: La fórmula vertebral para el holotipo de A. louisae es de 15 vértebras cervicales, 10 dorsales, 5, sacras y 82 caudales.

facts.statement: Like its close relative Supersaurus, Apatosaurus had high neural spines representing more than half the height of its vertebrae.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus, al igual que su pariente cercano Supersaurus, tiene espinas neurales altas, que representan más de la mitad de la altura de sus vértebras.

facts.statement: Like other diplodocids, its tail transformed into a whip-like structure at the tip.
facts.quote: Al igual que en otros diplodócidos, la cola se transformaba en una estructura en forma de látigo hacia su extremo.

facts.statement: It had a single large claw on each forelimb, a trait shared by all sauropods more derived than Shunosaurus.
facts.quote: Apatosaurus tenía una sola garra grande en cada extremidad anterior, una característica compartida por todos los saurópodos más derivados que Shunosaurus.

facts.statement: Its foot had three claws on the innermost toes, with a digital formula of 3-4-5-3-2.
facts.quote: El pie de Apatosaurus tiene tres garras en los dedos más internos, la fórmula digital es 3-4-5-3-2.

facts.statement: Its femurs were very robust, among the most robust femurs of any Sauropod member.
facts.quote: Los fémures de Apatosaurus son muy robustos, algunos de los más robustos fémures de cualquier miembro de Sauropoda.

facts.statement: Apatosaurus belongs to the parent group Apatosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Apatosaurinae

facts.statement: Apatosaurus is classified in the family Diplodocidae.
facts.quote: Family: Diplodocidae

facts.statement: Apatosaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Most size estimates for Apatosaurus are based on the type specimen of A. louisae, CM 3018.
facts.quote: La mayoría de las estimaciones del tamaño de Apatosaurus se basan en el espécimen tipo de A. louisae, CM 3018

facts.statement: In 1936, this specimen was measured at 21.8 meters based on the vertebral column.
facts.quote: En 1936, este ejemplar se midió en 21,8 m , mediante la medición de la columna vertebral.

facts.statement: Estimates vary slightly from the previous result, ranging from 21 to 22.8 meters in length and 16.1 to 22.4 tonnes in weight.
facts.quote: Las estimaciones varían muy poco del anterior resultado, entre unos 21 y 22,8 metros de largo y con un peso de entre 16,1 a 22,4 toneladas de peso.

facts.statement: A 2015 study estimated that CM 3018 would weigh between 21.8 and 38.2 tonnes based on volumetric models, similar in mass to the Argentine titanosaur Dreadnoughtus.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2015 calculó la masa corporal de algunos saurópodos sobre la base de modelos volumétricos, estimando que CM 3018 pesaría entre 21,8 y 38,2 toneladas, similar en masa a un titanosario argentino llamado Dreadnoughtus.

facts.statement: Some giant Apatosaurus specimens found in Oklahoma represent individuals approximately 11–30% longer, such as OMNH 1670, suggesting a mass possibly between 33 and 73 tonnes.
